rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation in max_reduction_dim2_kernel only executes when reduction_dim==2. With dim2=256, block_size=256: original elements_per_thread=1, mutant elements_per_thread=0. Zero causes no elements processed, outputting -FLT_MAX. Layer 2 bitwise equality across 112 rounds proves dim=2 was never tested (otherwise massive -FLT_MAX vs real max differences would appear).
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation resides exclusively in max_reduction_dim2_kernel, which is only invoked when the model is initialized with dim=2. All 112 rounds of Layer 2 testing showed bitwise equality, which is only possible if the model configuration used dim=1 throughout testing. Under dim=1 configuration, the mutated code path is never executed, making the mutation observationally equivalent. The mutation would cause catastrophic failure (outputting -FLT_MAX instead of actual maximums) if dim=2 were used.
rounds.kill_strategy: Initialize model with dim=2 and provide any input where true maximum along dimension 2 exceeds -FLT_MAX. The mutant will output -FLT_MAX (~-3.4e38) while the original outputs correct max values. Even uniform values of 1.0 would show massive divergence.
rounds.recommendations: EMD Layer 2 testing should cover ALL code paths by testing different model configurations (both dim=1 and dim=2), not just varying input values. Critical mutations in alternative execution branches can escape detection when only one configuration is tested.

rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should explicitly test all configurable code paths. For kernels with multiple modes (like dim=1 vs dim=2), generate mutants for each mode and ensure test configurations exercise all paths. Consider parameterized testing that sweeps configuration options.
